instruction: Apartment Floor Plate Subdivision Use the opened Bonsai IFC authoring environment to modify /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc by subdividing the apartment floor plate and exporting zone areas. You may use /home/user/Desktop/init_plan.png as a local reference image. Save the outputs as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc and /home/user/Desktop/result.csv. The IFC4 model must contain one project, one site, one building, and one storey named Level 1; ten spaces; twelve walls; one slab; eight doors; eight openings; eight void relationships; and eight fill relationships. Do not include windows, proxies, furniture, roofs, columns, beams, stairs, or flow terminals, and keep every IfcRoot GlobalId unique. Create spaces named A Living, A Bed, B Living, B Bed, C Living, C Bed, D Living, D Bed, South Corridor, and North Corridor. A Living, A Bed, B Living, C Living, C Bed, and D Living must each be 4.60 m by 4.60 m by 2.80 m. B Bed and D Bed must each be 4.40 m by 4.60 m by 2.80 m. South Corridor must be 19.40 m by 1.60 m by 2.80 m, and North Corridor must be 19.40 m by 1.40 m by 2.80 m. Assign all spaces to Level 1. The CSV must use the exact headers SpaceName, Zone, Level, NetFloorArea and contain one row for each final space. Report A Bed and A Living in Zone A with NetFloorArea 21.16 each; B Bed and B Living in Zone B with NetFloorArea 20.24 and 21.16; C Bed and C Living in Zone C with NetFloorArea 21.16 each; D Bed and D Living in Zone D with NetFloorArea 20.24 and 21.16; and North Corridor and South Corridor in Zone Corridor with NetFloorArea 27.16 and 31.04. Every row must use Level 1. Other representation details may vary. [Software] Bonsai workflows are used together with Blender; start Blender with `blender` (adjust path if needed).
